questions.prompt: Find the coordinate vector of \((3, -2)\) in the standard basis of \(\mathbb R^2\).
questions.answer: In the standard basis \(e_1\) = \((1,0)\), \(e_2\) = \((0,1)\), we have \((3, -2)\) = 3e1 - 2e2. Therefore the coordinate vector is \((3, -2)\).

questions.prompt: Find the coordinate vector of \(p(x)=4-x+2x^2\) in the basis \(\{1,x,x^2\}\).
questions.answer: The coordinate vector in the basis \(\{1,x,x^2\}\) is the list of coefficients in that order. Since \(p(x)=4-x+2x^2\), the coordinates are \((4, -1, 2)\).
We need \(a(1,1)+b(1,-1)=(3,1)\). This gives \((a+b,a-b)=(3,1)\). Solve \(a+b=3\) and \(a-b=1\). Adding gives \(2a=4\), so \(a=2\). Then \(b=1\). Therefore \([v]_B=(2,1)\).

questions.prompt: If \([v]_B=(2,-1)\) and \(B=\big((1,2),(3,0)\big)\), find \(v\) in standard coordinates.
Find the coordinates of \(p(x)=5+2(x-1)-3(x-1)^2\) in the basis \(\{1,x-1,(x-1)^2\}\).
questions.answer: The polynomial is already written as a linear combination of the basis vectors in order: \(5\cdot1+2(x-1)-3(x-1)^2\). Therefore its coordinate vector in this basis is \((5,2,-3)\).

questions.prompt: Find the standard polynomial for coordinate vector \((1, -2, 3)\) in basis \(\{1,x,x^2\}\).
questions.answer: The coordinate vector \((1,-2,3)\) means \(1\cdot1+(-2)x+3x^2\). Therefore the polynomial is \(1-2x+3x^2\).

questions.prompt: Let \(B=\big(1+x,1-x\big)\) for \(P_1\). Find the B-coordinates of \(p(x)=3+x\).
questions.answer: We need \(a(1+x)+b(1-x)=3+x\). Expanding gives \((a+b)+(a-b)x=3+x\). Therefore \(a+b=3\) and \(a-b=1\). Adding gives \(2a=4\), so \(a=2\). Then \(b=1\). Therefore \([p]_B=(2,1)\).

questions.prompt: Explain why coordinates depend on the chosen basis using \(v=(1,1)\), the standard basis, and \(B=\big((1,1),(1,-1)\big)\).
questions.answer: In the standard basis, \(v=1(1,0)+1(0,1)\), so its coordinates are \((1,1)\). In the basis \(B=\big((1,1),(1,-1)\big)\), the same vector is \(v=1(1,1)+0(1,-1)\), so its coordinates are \((1,0)\). The vector has not changed, but the coordinate description changes with the basis.

questions.prompt: A learner says the coordinate vector is the vector itself. Diagnose the error.
questions.answer: A coordinate vector records the coefficients of a vector relative to a chosen ordered basis. The same vector can have different coordinate vectors in different bases. For example, \((1,1)\) has coordinates \((1,1)\) in the standard basis of \(\mathbb R^2\), but coordinates \((1,0)\) in the basis (\((1,1)\), \((1,-1)\)). Therefore coordinates are a representation of the vector, not the vector itself.
